report.summary: Audited visible slice of daedalus/skills.py. Found docstring claim violation in parse_frontmatter: function promises SkillError with EVERY problem found, but early return on frontmatter size/line limits prevents reporting of further parse errors (e.g., invalid keys, duplicates). The rest of the module (load_skill, discover, etc.) is not visible, so completeness of malformed reporting and concurrency safety cannot be verified. No execution risks in visible code.
risks: parse_frontmatter raises SkillError with only size-related reasons if MAX_FRONTMATTER_BYTES or MAX_FRONTMATTER_LINES exceeded, stopping before collecting other issues. This contradicts the docstring guarantee that every problem is reported.
Visibility is limited; key functions like load_skill and discover are not provided, so their correctness and error handling are unknown.
todos: Refactor parse_frontmatter to defer size-check errors until after the block is fully parsed, so the SkillError includes all found issues.
Review load_skill and discover for concurrency and atomicity on Windows, and for adherence to the 'malformed is reported, never silently skipped' claim.

handoff.suggestion: In parse_frontmatter, move the size/line checks to a point before raising, but after the main loop has collected all other reasons. For example, collect the size reasons into a separate list and merge them before the final raise. Ensure the docstring claim of 'every problem' is true.
